summary: Iteration 3 backend + frontend regression. All 12 backend pytest tests pass (shipping options, quote endpoint w/ free-shipping threshold, quantity validation 1-5, session-with-shipping persistence, rate limit 5/hour per IP). Frontend: buy block, cart drawer, checkout wizard (validation, review, pay), Stripe redirect, and success polling all work as specified. TWO real bugs found: cart is destroyed on any page reload (CartContext localStorage race), and /checkout reload always bounces to '/' even when the cart is persisted.

ui_bugs.issue: Cart is wiped from localStorage on every page reload. The write-back useEffect (that persists `items` to localStorage) fires on mount with the initial [] value and overwrites the persisted data BEFORE the hydration useEffect's setItems has re-rendered. Repro: add item → confirm localStorage['nfl.cart.v1'] contains [{...}] → reload → localStorage now contains '[]' and nav-bag-count is gone.

Reloading /checkout (or direct-navigating to /checkout with cart persisted in localStorage) always bounces to /. Root cause: Checkout's `useEffect(() => { if (items.length === 0) navigate('/') })` fires before CartProvider's hydration effect (children effects run before parent effects in React). Compounds with the persistence bug — user cannot recover an in-progress checkout.

action_items: FIX CartContext persistence race (HIGH): Add a `hydrated` ref that starts false; the hydration effect sets it true after reading localStorage; the write-back effect must skip until `hydrated.current === true`. Otherwise the initial mount write of items=[] destroys any persisted cart.

FIX Checkout empty-cart bounce (HIGH): Do not redirect on the very first render — either wait a tick, gate on a `cartReady` flag from CartContext, or only redirect after cart has finished hydrating (e.g. expose `hydrated` from context and gate the redirect useEffect on it). Currently /checkout reload always bounces users home.
Consider clearing/prefixing waitlist test data (TEST_rl_…) if running multiple iterations.
critical_code_review_comments: CartContext.js: the hydrate effect and the write-back effect race on mount. write-back runs with the stale initial [] value from the closure and overwrites localStorage before the setItems from hydration commits. Standard fix: `const hydrated = useRef(false)` set true at end of hydrate effect; write-back returns early when !hydrated.current.
Checkout.js line 60: `if (items.length === 0 && !redirecting) navigate('/')` runs on first render before CartProvider hydration. Should be gated on a `hydrated` flag from CartContext.
Checkout.js uses `analytics.checkoutStep(...)` but there is no observable side-effect test — spot-check via console posthog.__loaded true confirmed.

rca of the issue: 1) Cart persistence loss: CartContext.js has two useEffects — a hydrate-from-localStorage effect and a write-items-to-localStorage effect. Both are declared in the same component with `[items]` and `[]` deps respectively. On mount, both fire in declaration order; the hydrate effect calls setItems(hydrated), but the second effect's closure still sees items=[] and writes '[]' to localStorage before the setItems from #1 causes a re-render. Fix: gate the write-back with a `hydrated` ref that becomes true only after the hydrate effect finishes reading localStorage. 2) /checkout reload bounce: The Checkout page's redirect useEffect (`if items.length === 0 → navigate('/')`) runs before the CartProvider's hydration effect fires (React effects run bottom-up, children first). Even if the persistence bug is fixed, the redirect will still fire on the very first render with the initial empty cart. Fix: expose a `hydrated` boolean from CartContext and gate the redirect on `hydrated && items.length === 0`.
